title: Export a task's full log as JSON or Markdown
plan:
Add task export endpoint and formatting logic to allow downloading a task's full log as JSON or Markdown, plus frontend client and UI to trigger downloads. Include a pure service for formatting and vitest tests for markdown formatting.
1. Add backend export service (new)
2. Add backend API route to router.ts
3. Add frontend client download API function
4. Add Download log UI to TaskView.tsx
requirements: Add GET /api/task/:taskId/export?format=json|markdown route with same auth/access checks as other task routes
Default format is json; supported values 'json' and 'markdown' otherwise respond 400 with { error }
For json: response is a pretty-printed JSON body { task: <task detail>, metrics, events } and sets Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="task-<first8>.<json>" and appropriate Content-Type

For markdown: produce readable transcript as specified (title with issue number/title, metrics summary: duration, LLM calls, tool calls, cost; events grouped by step with headings '## Step N — <description>', tool calls as bullets with tool name + short args, agent thoughts as blockquotes). Set Content-Disposition filename .md and Content-Type
Put formatting logic into new backend/src/services/taskExport.ts as pure functions, using .js extensions for backend imports
Add vitest tests for the markdown formatter in backend/src/services/__tests__/taskExport.test.ts covering key formatting behaviors
Add frontend API function exportTaskLog(taskId, format) in frontend/src/api/client.ts that downloads the file via fetch->blob->object URL->temporary <a download>
Add a Download log control in frontend/src/pages/TaskView.tsx offering JSON and Markdown options that call exportTaskLog
Ensure npx tsc -b passes in backend and frontend (noUncheckedIndexedAccess and other TS settings respected)
Unit tests for markdown formatter run under backend test suite
Use existing auth and access checks for task export route (same as other task routes)
summary:
Added task export functionality. Created backend/src/services/taskExport.ts with pure functions toJson and eventsToMarkdown and tests backend/src/services/__tests__/taskExport.test.ts verifying markdown output. Added GET /api/task/:taskId/export route in backend/src/api/router.ts which performs same access checks as other task routes, supports ?format=json|markdown (default json), returns 404 for missing task, 400 for unsupported formats, sets Content-Disposition and Content-Type, and uses the service for formatting. Frontend: added exportTaskLog(taskId, format) in frontend/src/api/client.ts which downloads the file via blob and temporary anchor. Added Download JSON / MD buttons to frontend/src/pages/TaskView.tsx that call exportTaskLog. Verified by running backend TypeScript build and tests: backend tsc passed after fixes; ran backend tests—added tests run and passed (one initial failure fixed). Frontend tsc build passed.

Requirements:
1. R1: GET /api/task/:taskId/export implemented in backend/src/api/router.ts
2. R2: Default format json and 400 for unsupported - router validates query.format
3. R3: 404 on unknown task - router checks registry/checkpoint/db and returns 404
4. R4: JSON export returns pretty-printed JSON, Content-Disposition and Content-Type set - implemented using taskExport.toJson and headers
5. R5: Markdown export via taskExport.eventsToMarkdown produces title, metrics summary, events grouped by step with tool calls and agent thoughts; Content-Disposition and Content-Type set
6. R6: Formatting logic placed in backend/src/services/taskExport.ts using .js imports in router
7. R7: Vitest tests added at backend/src/services/__tests__/taskExport.test.ts covering markdown formatting
8. R8: Frontend exportTaskLog added in frontend/src/api/client.ts that downloads blob via temporary anchor
9. R9: Download controls added to frontend/src/pages/TaskView.tsx calling exportTaskLog
10. R10: Type-check: backend and frontend tsc builds passed
11. R11: Unit tests for markdown formatter included and run under backend test suite
12. R12: Route uses same auth/assertTaskAccess as other task routes (assertTaskAccess used)
